title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
statement: Given a BST and two existing nodes p and q, return their lowest common ancestor.
explanation: Walk left when both values are smaller, right when both are larger; otherwise the current node is the split point.

title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Tree
statement: Given a binary tree and two existing nodes, return their lowest common ancestor.
explanation: Return a target when found; combine left and right recursive results. A node with hits from both sides is the LCA.

title: Product of Array Except Self
statement: Return an array where each value is the product of all input values except itself, without division.
explanation: Store prefix products in the output, then multiply by a running suffix product.

title: Sliding Window Maximum
statement: Return the maximum for each contiguous window of size k.
explanation: Maintain indices in decreasing-value order, removing expired indices and smaller trailing values.

title: Search a 2D Matrix II
statement: Search a row-wise and column-wise sorted matrix for target.
explanation: Start at the top-right; move left if too large and down if too small.

title: Valid Anagram
statement: Return whether two strings are anagrams.
explanation: Reject unequal lengths, then compare character frequency counts.
example: s='anagram', t='nagaram' -> true; s='rat', t='car' -> false

title: Missing Number
statement: Find the missing value from the distinct integers in [0,n].
explanation: XOR all indices and values; paired values cancel, leaving the missing integer.

title: Find the Duplicate Number
statement: Find the duplicate in an array of n+1 values in [1,n] without modifying the array.
explanation: Count values at most mid; a count greater than mid means the duplicate lies in the lower half.

title: Find Median from Data Stream
statement: Design addNum and findMedian for a stream of integers.
explanation: Keep a max-heap for the lower half and min-heap for the upper half, balanced so lower has at most one extra item.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
statement: Return the length of a strictly increasing subsequence.
explanation: Maintain minimal tails for each subsequence length and binary-search the first tail not smaller than each value.
